az_high_rappel_area.blurb: High Rappel Area sits in the Granite Dells near Prescott in central Arizona, at roughly 5,200 feet. Its Main Wall is called perhaps the most striking wall in the Dells, and the area breaks into sub-walls such as Main Wall Left, Main Wall Right and Sean's Wall. Trad is the main style, with a smaller group of sport routes and a couple of boulder problems. Grades run from easy fifth class up through the 5.12s, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.11. Across the Dells, the rock is medium-grained desert granite that turns grainy on some formations.

az_reef_of_rocks.blurb: Reef of Rocks lies on the Upper Highway of Mount Lemmon, in the Santa Catalina Mountains near Tucson. Its formations Neptune and Aegir sit near 7,500 feet and are known for steep red wall routes, with several multi-pitch lines among them. Neptune, Aegir and Poseidon hold most of the climbs. Trad leads, backed by a solid sport group and a handful of boulder problems. Grades are mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with a good number of 5.13s and a few 5.14s. The Upper Highway as a whole is likely to be very cold, or under snow, in winter months.

ar_crystal_bluff.blurb: Crystal Bluff is an urban crag in North Little Rock, perched above the Arkansas River and about five minutes from downtown. The rock is quartzitic sandstone, and its blocky breaks make good crimps and edges. Nearly everything is sport, with only a few trad lines. Routes are short, roughly 30 to 75 feet or a bit more, and the average grade falls around 5.9 to 5.10a, with the spread running from 5.6 to 5.12 and most climbs at 5.9 to 5.11. The climbing ranges from bouldery cruxes to power-endurance. Capitol Crag holds the most climbs, followed by Main Street and Vestal.

ar_fitzgerald_mountain.blurb: Fitzgerald Mountain is in Springdale, about 13 miles from downtown Fayetteville in Northwest Arkansas. It is a mountain biking area with rock formations along several trails, and climbing development is still in its early stages. Sport is the main style, with a good number of boulder problems and very little trad. Sport grades run mostly 5.9 to 5.11 and reach 5.12, and the boulders sit at V1 to V3. Fitzgerald South Area holds the most climbs; it faces west and is shaded by tree canopy, with routes of 25 to 50 feet. Fitzgerald North is mostly boulder problems.

ca_sherman_pass_road.blurb: Sherman Pass Road climbing sits in the Kern River Sierra, with Kernville and Kennedy Meadows as the nearest towns. Sport leads and trad adds a solid share. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, mostly 5.10 and 5.11. Rodeo Flat holds the most climbs: it lies on the Kern Plateau near 7,300 feet, with three crags in a small gorge cut by Fish Creek and two on the ridge above the flat, taking in sport, trad and top-rope. At Spirit Rock, near 7,500 feet, there are single and multi-pitch routes from 5.7 to 5.11, mostly sport, and it is described as good summer climbing.

co_arthur_s_rock.blurb: Arthur's Rock rises in Lory State Park, west of Fort Collins, at about 6,300 feet. Bouldering is the main draw, with climbing that is fingery and footwork-heavy, on small edges and gritty slopers. A smaller collection of trad and sport routes sits mostly on the South Face, an overhanging dome 150 to 200 feet tall where the routes mostly follow crack systems, and at the Overlook. Boulder grades run from V0 through V12, with most problems in the lower and middle range. The hillside faces south and is sunny, which suits winter, spring and fall, while summer is generally too hot. Main Area, South Face of Arthur's Rock and Fog that Surrounds hold the most climbs.
